finding.claim: picomatch.test returns match=true whenever input string equals glob string without running the regex, so a pattern like "[abc]" incorrectly matches the literal input "[abc]".
finding.title: input-equals-glob shortcut bypasses regex

verifier.reason: picomatch.test at picomatch.js:139 sets match=input===glob and at picomatch.js:147 only runs the regex when match is false or capture is true, so input '[abc]' equal to glob '[abc]' returns Boolean(match)=true at picomatch.js:155 without regex execution.

finding.claim: Last token value is only assigned when prevIndex is truthy, so for inputs with a leading slash where prevIndex is 0 the assignment is skipped and tokens keep an empty value.
finding.title: tokens assignment uses falsy check for index 0

verifier.reason: The condition at scan.js:390 requires prevIndex to be truthy before assigning the final token at scan.js:391, and scan.js:380-383 sets prevIndex to the slash index i, so a sole leading slash leaves prevIndex as 0 and the final assignment is skipped.

finding.claim: With opts.noext=true both isExtglob and isGlob are cleared, so a plain glob like "*.js" is incorrectly reported as non-glob even though noext should only disable extglobs.
finding.title: noext clears isGlob

verifier.reason: The block at scan.js:301-304 unconditionally clears both isExtglob and isGlob when opts.noext is true, and the cleared isGlob is then used for the base/glob split at scan.js:316-324 and reported in state at scan.js:340-352, so non-extglob glob detection such as the bracket case at scan.js:242-243 is also erased.

finding.claim: The single-dot check does code=advance() inside the condition, so when the second char is not a dot the lookahead char is consumed and never examined for comma handling, missing e.g. the comma in "{a.,b}".
finding.title: dot lookahead consumes following char

verifier.reason: At scan.js:113 the lookahead is assigned to the same `code` variable, and the immediately following non-else check at scan.js:125 tests that same `code` for CHAR_COMMA, so in "{a.,b}" the comma consumed as lookahead is examined and triggers the comma branch.
